strangers_child.text: There's a whole room of old toys upstairs. Dolls' houses and rocking horses. I'm not allowed to ride the rocking horse. I asked four times.

strangers_curator.text: Strangers' Hall is a merchant's house, some parts six hundred years old. It's named after the Strangers: the Flemish and Walloon weavers Norwich invited in 1565.

then.text: You've come about the canaries? Ah. The Strangers brought caged canaries from the Low Countries, and Norwich went canary-mad. Weavers bred them at their looms. The Norwich canary is still a breed: big, plump and golden.
When the football club changed to yellow and green in 1907, there was only ever going to be one nickname. Here: take the chorus leader a word from me. She's out on the market.

else.text: They made bombazine, a fine silk-and-wool cloth, and thousands of other new fabrics. Norwich got very rich, very fast. They also got the canaries. Ask at Carrow Road about those.
